findings.title: Request/response expectation pairs the request with the wrong response when matching events arrive in a burst (request_id overwritten by a second handler task)
findings.bug_class: race / double-dispatch (handler removes itself only after it has been scheduled)
findings.scenario: `async with tab.expect_request(r'.*/img\d+\.png') as exp: await tab.get(page_with_many_images)`, then `await exp.request` and `await exp.response` (or `response_body`). Listener.listener_loop starts every callback with asyncio.create_task and drains queued inbox messages without yielding. So several matching Network.requestWillBeSent events each get their own _request_handler task before the first one runs and removes the handler. Task 1 sets request_id=A and resolves request_future with A. Task 2 then sets request_id=B (line 44) before set_result raises InvalidStateError. From then on _response_handler and _loading_finished_handler match request B. `exp.request`/`RequestExpectation.value` return request A while `exp.response`, `ResponseExpectation.value` and `response_body` return B's response and body. Each extra task also ends in an unretrieved InvalidStateError. DownloadExpectation._handler (line 206) and BaseFetchInterception._response_handler (intercept.py:35) use the same self-removing pattern and get the same InvalidStateError tasks on bursts. examples/wait_for_page.py uses exactly this kind of broad pattern (`https://github.githubassets.com/assets/.*`).
findings.why_tests_miss: test_expect_request, test_expect_response and test_expect_response_with_reload in tests/core/test_tab.py only match the single top-level document URL, so only one event ever matches. No test matches a pattern that hits several subresources, and no test compares request.url with response.url.
findings.repro_idea: Serve a page with 40 . Inside `tab.expect_request(r'.*/img\d+\.png\?t=.*')`, compare `(await exp.request).url` with `(await exp.response).url`, and install a loop exception handler to count InvalidStateError.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/detect-A10/probe_expect_race.py against real headless Chromium: 8/8 trials mismatched (e.g. `request: img0.png?t=0 response: img15.png?t=0 MISMATCH`), and the loop exception handler logged 89 `InvalidStateError('invalid state')`. Code path traced: connection.py Listener.listener_loop calls `asyncio.create_task(callback(*args))` for each event, and _receive_message uses `self._inbox.get()`, which returns without suspending while items are queued.

findings.title: tab.intercept() cannot be nested or combined with other Fetch users: inner enable replaces the outer patterns, the outer handler takes the inner request, and the inner teardown makes Fetch re-enable with no patterns, pausing every request
findings.bug_class: shared tab-wide state clobbered / missing event filtering
findings.scenario: (1) `async with tab.intercept('*a.json*', REQUEST, XHR) as a: async with tab.intercept('*b.json*', REQUEST, XHR) as b: await tab.get(page_fetching_a_and_b)`. The inner Fetch.enable([b]) replaces the tab's pattern list, so a.json is never paused. _response_handler accepts any Fetch.requestPaused without checking its own pattern, so both a and b resolve with b.json. `await a.request` returns b.json, `a.continue_request()` continues b's request, and `b.continue_request()` raises ProtocolException. (2) The inner block exits before the outer one has matched: _teardown sends Fetch.disable, which turns off interception for the whole tab and removes fetch from manually_enabled_domains. The outer RequestPaused handler is still registered, so the next tab.send() goes through Connection._register_handlers, which sends `fetch.enable()` with no patterns. Every request, including the document, now pauses. `tab.get()` hangs, the outer interception resolves with the page document instead of a.json, and the page's XHRs never complete. The same happens when a user-installed RequestPaused handler with its own Fetch.enable coexists with tab.intercept().

findings.title: Timing out a wait on expectation.value/request/response/response_body cancels the shared future, so later awaits raise CancelledError and the expectation is dead
findings.bug_class: cancellation of a shared future (missing asyncio.shield)
findings.function: ResponseExpectation.value / RequestExpectation.value / BaseRequestExpectation.request, response, response_body; BaseFetchInterception.request, response_body, continue_request, fulfill_request, fail_request, continue_response
findings.scenario: `async with tab.expect_response(r'.*/page1') as exp: try: await asyncio.wait_for(exp.value, 0.5) except TimeoutError: pass; await tab.get(url_page1); await exp.value` → raises CancelledError, although the response arrived and nothing cancelled the caller (`current_task().cancelling() == 0`). The property awaits the bare stored future (`return await self.response_future`). When wait_for cancels the waiting task, asyncio also cancels that future. When the event arrives later, the handler's set_result raises InvalidStateError in a background task. This applies to intercept.py as well: after a timed-out `wait_for(interception.request, t)`, `interception.continue_request()` raises CancelledError. The paused request can then only be released by leaving the block, and the CancelledError tends to escape `except Exception` blocks and look like task cancellation. The repo's own tests use exactly this pattern (`asyncio.wait_for(request_info.value, timeout=3)`).
findings.why_tests_miss: Tests always await the expectation after the event has already happened or within the timeout, so the wait_for never fires and the future is never cancelled. No test re-awaits an expectation after a timeout.
findings.repro_idea: As in the scenario: wait_for(exp.value, 0.5) with nothing loading, then trigger the navigation and await exp.value again. Expect CancelledError plus a loop-handler InvalidStateError.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/detect-A10/probe_cancel.py printed `response_future state after timeout: <Future cancelled>`, `LOOP ERR: InvalidStateError('invalid state')`, and `second wait raised CancelledError although the response arrived ... cancelling(): 0`. The first run of the intercept probe showed `intercept.py line 123, in continue_request ... asyncio.exceptions.CancelledError` after an earlier timed-out `wait_for(a.request, 5)`.

findings.title: Chrome hangs once its stdout/stderr PIPE fills: _start_process opens pipes that nothing reads while the browser runs
findings.scenario: browser = await zendriver.start(headless=True, browser_args=['--enable-logging=stderr']); then a page that logs to the console in a loop (e.g. tab.get(data: URL with console.error(...)) about 200 times). _start_process launches Chrome with stdout=PIPE and stderr=PIPE. During normal operation nothing reads those pipes (the only reader is _read_process_stderr, on the connect-failure path). Once about 64KB of stderr has piled up, Chrome's next log write blocks in the kernel. The browser process stops servicing CDP, so every tab.get/evaluate/send after that hangs forever unless the caller adds a timeout. With default flags the same thing happens in any session that writes 64KB of Chrome ERROR lines over its lifetime, such as TLS handshake failures, GPU/dbus errors or GCM registration errors.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test runs Chrome with stderr logging, and none runs long enough to emit 64KB of stderr. With default flags this container's Chrome writes only about 5KB at startup and then nothing (measured), so the suite never gets near the pipe limit. No test checks how full the pipe is.
findings.repro_idea: Probe in scratch dir probe_pipe.py: start(headless=True, browser_args=['--enable-logging=stderr']). Loop up to 400 times over tab.get(data URL with console.error('x'.repeat(200))) + tab.evaluate('1+1'), each step under wait_for(10). Use ioctl FIONREAD on browser._process.stderr to watch the pending byte count, and read /proc/<pid>/wchan when it hangs.
findings.evidence: Probe output: 'iteration 180: ok stderr pending=56570', 'iteration 200: ok stderr pending=62170', 'iteration 204: TIMEOUT, stderr pending=63010', 'wchan: anon_pipe_write'. The Chrome browser process was blocked writing to the full stderr pipe, and tab.get/evaluate timed out from then on. Control run with default flags: pending stayed at 4982 bytes for 200 iterations. grep: the only reads of _process.stderr/stdout are in _read_process_stderr (browser.py:589, connect-failure path).

findings.title: Forwarder leaks tunnels to an authenticated https:// upstream after Chrome closes the connection, because the close is never passed upstream
findings.scenario: Call browser.create_context(proxy_server='https://user:pass@proxy:443'), browse, then let Chrome close a tunnelled connection (tab or context closed, idle socket dropped). copy_stream(client->upstream) reads EOF and calls write_eof() only if writer.can_write_eof(). An asyncio SSL transport returns False there, so the upstream proxy is never told and the tunnel stays up. pipe() gathers both directions, so it keeps waiting for upstream->client to reach EOF. Meanwhile the _handle_client task, the half-open client socket, the TLS upstream socket, the upstream proxy's tunnel and the origin connection all stay alive until the remote side times out (minutes for TLS or HTTP/2 origins, since Chromium does not send close_notify). With an http:// or socks5 upstream the FIN is forwarded and everything is torn down at once. Long scraping sessions through https proxies pile up these connections.
findings.why_tests_miss: test_proxy.py runs the forwarder only against plain-TCP http and socks5 fake proxies. There is no end-to-end test with an https (TLS) upstream, and no test checks that tasks or sockets are released after the client disconnects.
findings.repro_idea: Run a TLS CONNECT proxy (self-signed cert) whose origin closes on EOF. Build ProxyForwarder(UpstreamProxy.from_url('https://u:p@127.0.0.1:port', insecure_ctx)), open a CONNECT tunnel, close the client socket, sleep 2s, then check len(forwarder._client_tasks).
findings.evidence: Scratch proxy_probe.py: 'tls=False: forwarder client tasks still alive 2s after client closed: 0' and 'tls=True: forwarder client tasks still alive 2s after client closed: 1', with the same fake proxy and origin in both runs. The only difference is the TLS upstream.

The same happens with cd.setdefault('s', {'b': 1}) and `cd |= {'o': {'b': 1}}`. findings.title: copy.copy() or pickling a ContraDict gives an object that still returns deleted keys as attributes
findings.bug_class: broken invariant after reconstruction (__dict__ is not self)
findings.scenario: __init__ makes the instance __dict__ the dict itself (`super().__setattr__('__dict__', self)`). copy.copy and pickle rebuild through __reduce_ex__ without calling __init__: they create a separate real __dict__ and copy every item into it as state (the state is the dict itself), then set the items again. After `c = copy.copy(cd); del c['a']`, `'a' in c` is False but `c.a` still returns the old value, because __getattribute__ falls through to object.__getattribute__, which finds the stale entry in the separate __dict__. `c.pop('a')` behaves the same, and vars(c) is stale. This affects e.g. copy.copy(element.attrs), copy.copy(browser.info), or a ContraDict sent through multiprocessing.
findings.why_tests_miss: ContraDict has no tests, and nothing in the test suite copies or pickles one.
findings.repro_idea: c = copy.copy(ContraDict({'a': {'b': 1}})); del c['a']; print(c.a)  # prints {'b': 1} instead of raising AttributeError. pickle.loads(pickle.dumps(...)) does the same.
findings.evidence: Scratch cd_probe.py: 'after del c5['a'] (copy.copy), c5.a -> {'b': 1}', 'after del c7['a'], c7.a -> {'b': 1}' (pickle), 'vars(copy) is copy -> False'. deepcopy is not affected (memo makes the state the new object).

findings.title: Proxy forwarder drops the client connection without an HTTP error, and logs an unhandled-exception traceback, when encoding or parsing raises something other than ProxyError

With a socks5 upstream, a CONNECT or GET to a host that has a DNS label over 63 characters or an empty label (e.g. 'a..b.com') makes encode_socks5_address raise UnicodeError from host.encode('idna') (line 337). open_tunnel re-raises it unchanged, _handle_client lets it escape, the client gets an empty response instead of the 502 used for every other upstream failure, and asyncio logs 'ERROR asyncio: Unhandled exception in client_connected_cb' with a full traceback. ValueError from urlsplit or url.port on malformed targets (non-CONNECT path, line 263/274) goes the same way.

findings.title: Assigning an existing ContraDict or list to a ContraDict stores a copy, so later changes to the original are not seen
findings.scenario: _wrap always rebuilds mappings (cls(v)) and non-str sequences (a new list), even when v is already a ContraDict or a list. So `inner = cdict(); cd.child = inner; inner.x = 1; cd.child` gives {} and `cd.child is inner` is False. Likewise `lst = []; cd.l = lst; lst.append(1); cd.l` gives []. Plain dict assignment keeps the reference, which the docstring ('directly inherited from dict') suggests is also what ContraDict does. copy.copy() also turns into a deep copy for nested mappings (c.a is not cd.a).
findings.why_tests_miss: ContraDict has no tests.
findings.repro_idea: inner = ContraDict(); c = ContraDict(); c.child = inner; inner.x = 1; assert c.child == {}  # surprising
findings.evidence: Scratch cd_probe.py: 'c3.child after inner.x=1 -> {}', 'c3.l after lst.append -> []', 'copy.copy is shallow? c5.a is c4.a -> False'.

findings.title: open_tunnel reports a timed-out proxy handshake as 'proxy closed the connection' because TimeoutError is an OSError subclass
findings.scenario: On Python 3.11+, asyncio.TimeoutError is the builtin TimeoutError, which subclasses OSError. The isinstance(e, (OSError, IncompleteReadError)) check at line 112 therefore matches first, and the `isinstance(e, asyncio.TimeoutError)` branch at line 114 can never run. When an upstream proxy accepts TCP but never answers CONNECT or the SOCKS handshake within TIMEOUT, the warning logged by _handle_client says 'proxy closed the connection: TimeoutError()' instead of 'timed out waiting for the proxy', which misleads anyone debugging a slow proxy. The status (502) is the same.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test runs a handshake timeout (TIMEOUT is a 30s module constant).
findings.repro_idea: Set zendriver.core.proxy.TIMEOUT=0.5 and point UpstreamProxy at a server that accepts and never replies. Call open_tunnel('example.com', 443) and print str(ProxyError).
findings.evidence: Scratch proxy_probe.py on Python 3.13.16: 'handshake timeout -> 'proxy closed the connection: TimeoutError()''.

findings.title: Chrome stdout/stderr are piped but never read, so Chrome freezes once the stderr pipe fills
findings.scenario: zd.start(headless=True, browser_args=['--enable-logging=stderr']), then call tab.evaluate("console.log('x'.repeat(2000))") about 15 times. Chrome writes every log line to the stderr pipe, and nothing reads it: Browser.start reads stderr only on the failure path through util._read_process_stderr. When the pipe buffer fills, Chrome's writes block, the browser stops answering CDP, and every later tab call hangs. browser.stop() then hangs too (see the stop() finding). With default args the pipe also fills, more slowly: about 5 KB of dbus/GPU errors at startup plus about 150 bytes for each network or SSL error, so a long crawl can stall the same way.
findings.why_tests_miss: Test sessions are short and use default flags, so stderr stays far below the pipe capacity. test_connection_error_raises_exception_and_logs_stderr only covers the read on the failure path.
findings.repro_idea: Start with --enable-logging=stderr, loop tab.evaluate(console.log of 2 KB) wrapped in wait_for(…, 5), and read FIONREAD on browser._process.stderr when it times out.
findings.evidence: Probe p7_pipe.py: with --enable-logging=stderr, 'evaluate #15 timed out after 5.0s; unread stderr bytes=36931; process alive=True', then 'browser.stop() did not finish within 15s'. With default args: 5073 unread bytes right after start, rising to 5793 after 5 navigations to an expired-certificate page. The fix is stdout/stderr=DEVNULL, or a drain task or temp file kept for the failure message.

findings.title: Browser.stop() waits for CDP replies with no timeout before terminate()/kill(), and drops the atexit hook first
findings.scenario: Start a browser and use a tab, which attaches a flat session. The Chrome process then stops answering: it is hung, SIGSTOPped, or blocked on the full stderr pipe. Calling await browser.stop() first runs asyncio_atexit.unregister (line 870). _stop then awaits target.aclose() for each target (each sends Target.detachFromTarget through the browser connection) and connection.send(Browser.close), and none of these awaits has a timeout. stop() hangs forever and never reaches self._process.terminate()/kill(). If the caller wraps stop() in wait_for, the cancel leaves the process running and the temp profile in place, and because the atexit hook is already gone, nothing cleans up later.
findings.why_tests_miss: The stop tests (test_browser_stop_* and test_browser_stopped_is_true_when_stopped_externally) only use a responsive browser or one whose websocket is already closed. None of them uses a browser that is alive but not answering.
findings.repro_idea: os.kill(browser._process_pid, SIGSTOP) after tab.evaluate('1'), run asyncio.create_task(browser.stop()), and check after 8 s whether the task is done and whether the process was terminated.
findings.evidence: Probe p8_stop_hang.py: 'stop done after 8s? False | process terminated? None'. task.print_stack() showed it waiting on a Transaction with method Target.detachFromTarget, status pending.

findings.title: atexit cleanup always crashes at asyncio.to_thread(process.wait), leaking the temp profile of every browser not stopped explicitly
findings.scenario: asyncio.run(main()) where main does `b = await zd.start(); await b.get(...)` and never calls stop(). This is the documented fallback that Browser.create registers through asyncio_atexit. asyncio.run shuts down the default executor before loop.close(), and asyncio_atexit callbacks run inside loop.close(). _atexit_cleanup calls _stop, which terminates the process and then calls `await asyncio.to_thread(self._process.wait)`, which raises RuntimeError('Executor shutdown has been called'). _cleanup_temporary_profile never runs, so a /tmp/uc_* Chrome profile (often tens of MB) is left behind on every run. The same failure hits the _cleanup_temporary_profile call in _atexit_cleanup, because _stop raised first.
findings.why_tests_miss: Every test fixture calls browser.stop() explicitly (conftest CreateBrowser.__aexit__ and shared_browsers), so the atexit path never runs in tests. No test checks that the profile directory is removed.
findings.repro_idea: In a script, start a browser, record b.config.user_data_dir, return without stop(), then check after the interpreter exits whether the directory still exists.
findings.evidence: Probe p12_atexit.py printed 'Unhandled exception in asyncio atexit callback <bound method Browser._atexit_cleanup ...>: Executor shutdown has been called' and 'temp profile /tmp/uc_g8gnsv0r still exists'. The shared /tmp held more than 40 leaked uc_* directories from this session's probes.

findings.title: Cancelling or failing zd.start() after Chrome launches orphans the Chrome process and its temp profile (no atexit hook, Browser pinned in the registry)
findings.bug_class: resource-lifecycle / leak on cancel and error
findings.scenario: await asyncio.wait_for(zd.start(headless=True), 0.25), as a user would do to bound startup on a slow machine. Browser.start has already called util._start_process and util.get_registered_instances().add(self). The cancel arrives during the connection-retry loop (or later, for example in set_discover_targets or _read_headless_user_agent). Browser.start has no try/except around this section; it calls stop() only on the `if not self.info` path. Browser.create registers asyncio_atexit only after start() returns. As a result the Chrome process keeps running after the Python process exits, the uc_* profile stays, and the registry set holds a strong reference to the Browser. Any exception after launch has the same effect, for example a ProtocolException from set_discover_targets.
findings.why_tests_miss: test_connection_error_raises_exception_and_logs_stderr only covers the `not self.info` branch, which does call stop(). No test cancels start() or makes a later startup step fail.
findings.repro_idea: Call wait_for(zd.start(headless=True), 0.1) and wait_for(zd.start(headless=True), 0.25); after asyncio.run returns, check /proc/<pid> and the profile directories of util.get_registered_instances().
findings.evidence: Probe p2_cancel.py: both starts timed out, and 'registered browser pid 11139 running? True dir exists? True' (same for 11228). After the Python process exited: '11139 alive .../chromium dir exists True' and '11228 alive'. I killed both by hand.

findings.title: Printing or logging a template Config creates its temp user_data_dir, so browsers started from it share one profile; the second fails and its stop() deletes the first one's live profile
findings.scenario: config = zd.Config(headless=True); print(config) (or logger.info('%s', config)); b1 = await zd.start(config); b2 = await zd.start(config). __repr__ calls getattr(self, k) on every property, including user_data_dir, whose getter runs mkdtemp and stores the path on the template. Config.__init__ deliberately defers this 'so config can be used/reused as a template for multiple browser instances', and test_multiple_browsers relies on that. After repr, every deepcopy carries the same path with _custom_data_dir False. Chrome's process singleton makes b2's Chrome exit, so zd.start raises 'Failed to connect to browser', and b2's stop() then rmtree's the profile directory that b1 is still using.
findings.why_tests_miss: test_multiple_browsers_diff_userdata never calls repr or reads user_data_dir on the template before starting. No test checks that repr has no side effects.
findings.repro_idea: Run repr(config), then start two browsers from that config and check os.path.isdir(b1.config.user_data_dir) after the second start fails.
findings.evidence: Probe p3_repr.py: 'template before repr: None', 'template after repr: /tmp/uc_lygxj1ie custom? False', 'b2 start failed: Exception Failed to connect to browser', 'b1 profile dir still exists? False'.

findings.title: Temp profile dir leaks when start() fails before launch (bad executable) or cannot connect to an existing browser
findings.scenario: (a) zd.start(browser_executable_path='/nonexistent/chrome'): Browser.__init__ runs `logger.debug('Session object initialized: %s' % vars(self))` (line 274). The string is formatted even when debug logging is off, which runs Config.__repr__ and creates a uc_* directory. start() then raises FileNotFoundError and nothing removes the directory. (b) zd.start(host='127.0.0.1', port=<nothing listening>): start() calls self.config() (creating the temp dir), cannot connect, and calls self.stop(). _stop returns early at `if not self.connection and not self._process: return`, which skips _cleanup_temporary_profile. Each failed attempt (for example a retry loop) leaks one directory.
findings.why_tests_miss: The only connection-failure test patches test_connection on a launched process (so _process is set and _stop does not return early), and it never checks the profile directory. No test uses a bad executable path or a dead host:port.
findings.repro_idea: Set TMPDIR to an empty directory, attempt both failing starts, and list uc_* afterwards.
findings.evidence: Probe p1_leak.py: after the FileNotFoundError, one uc_g8d2vmf5 directory existed; after the 'Failed to connect to browser' attempt on port 1, a second one (uc_v76fong7) existed.

findings.title: Restarting a Browser never relaunches Chrome: start() saves the auto-chosen host and port in self.config and later treats them as 'connect to existing'
findings.scenario: (1) b = await zd.start(); await b.stop(); await b.start(). The first start wrote config.host='127.0.0.1' and config.port=free_port() (lines 534-535). On restart, `host is not None and port is not None` sets connect_existing=True, so no process is launched. test_connection fails, but self.info still holds the old /json/version data, so the `if not self.info` failure check is skipped. A Connection to the old ws URL then raises ConnectionRefusedError. (2) If the Chrome process died (crash, or the user closed the window), b.start() takes the branch built for exactly this case, `return await self.create(config=self.config)`. The new instance inherits host and port, also connects to the dead port, and raises 'Failed to connect to browser'. stop() also leaves self.targets, self.connection and self.info stale.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test calls start() again after stop() or after the process died. The tests stop at asserting browser.stopped.
findings.repro_idea: Run stop() then start(); separately, kill the process, call start(), and check whether a new pid appears.
findings.evidence: Probe p4_restart.py: 'stopped; config host/port still 127.0.0.1 59477 targets kept: 1', then 'restart after stop failed: ConnectionRefusedError(111, "Connect call failed ('127.0.0.1', 59477)") process launched? None', and 'restart after crash failed: Exception('... Failed to connect to browser ...')'.

findings.title: expect_request/expect_response mix two requests: request is the first match, response and body are the last, and the handler task raises InvalidStateError
findings.scenario: async with tab.expect_request(r'.*/data\?n=.*') as exp: await tab.get(page that starts 5 fetches at once). The Listener drains the session inbox without yielding and creates one handler task per RequestWillBeSent before any task runs, so _request_handler runs once per matching request. Self-removal does nothing for tasks already created. The first task sets request_future. Each later task overwrites self.request_id and then raises InvalidStateError from set_result. As a result exp.value/exp.request returns request n=0, while exp.response, response_body and loading_finished match request_id n=4. The user gets one request's headers together with another request's response and body. expect_response has the same mismatch.
findings.why_tests_miss: test_expect_request and test_expect_response use a pattern that matches exactly one request (the html file), so the handler never runs twice.
findings.repro_idea: Serve a page with 5 parallel fetch('/data?n=i') calls, then compare (await exp.value).request.url with (await exp.response).url and record loop exception-handler calls.
findings.evidence: Probe p6_expect.py, five trials: 'request.url=data?n=0 response.url=data?n=4 body='payload for /data?n=4' req_id=12211.2 exp.request_id=12211.6'. Result: 'mismatches 5'; the loop exception handler logged 20 InvalidStateError('invalid state').

findings.title: DownloadExpectation restores the browser-wide download behavior from per-tab state, wiping another tab's set_download_path
findings.bug_class: state-consistency / duplicated state disagrees with reality
findings.scenario: await tab1.set_download_path(dir) records the setting only on tab1 as tab1._download_behavior. Then tab2 = await browser.get(url, new_tab=True); async with tab2.expect_download(): click a download link. Browser.setDownloadBehavior applies to the whole browser context, but __init__ reads tab2._download_behavior (None), so __aexit__ resets the context to behavior='default' with no path. tab1._download_behavior still says ['allow', dir], so tab1.download_file() skips re-applying it, and tab1's downloads silently go to ~/Downloads instead of dir. Element.record_video sets 'allow' without updating _download_behavior, so its state also drifts.
findings.why_tests_miss: test_expect_download uses a single tab and never checks where later downloads land.
findings.repro_idea: Call set_download_path on tab1, run expect_download on tab2, then tab1.download_file(...) and list dir and ~/Downloads.
findings.evidence: Probe p10_download.py: before the expectation, 'before.bin' landed in dl_target. Afterwards 'tab1._download_behavior still says: ['allow', .../dl_target]', but the dl dir held only ['before.bin'] and after.bin appeared in ~/Downloads (removed after the probe).

findings.title: `async with await zd.start() as browser:` never stops the browser
findings.bug_class: resource-lifecycle / context manager does not release
findings.scenario: examples/wait_for_page.py shows `async with await zd.start() as browser:`. Browser.__aexit__ only re-raises exceptions; it never calls stop(). After the block the Chrome process, websocket, proxy forwarders and temp profile stay alive until the event loop closes, and the atexit path then leaks the profile (see the atexit finding). A loop that opens one browser per job with `async with` piles up Chrome processes. Connection.__aexit__ (used by `async with tab`) closes only the websocket.
findings.why_tests_miss: The tests use their own CreateBrowser context manager in conftest, whose __aexit__ calls stop(), so Browser.__aexit__ is never used for lifetime management.
findings.repro_idea: async with await zd.start(headless=True) as b: pass; then print(b.stopped, b._process_pid).
findings.evidence: Probe p5_aexit.py: 'after async with: stopped? False pid 11844'.

findings.title: Browser/Connection __aexit__ rebuild the exception as exc_type(exc_val), turning JSONDecodeError, ExceptionGroup and similar errors into TypeError
findings.bug_class: state-consistency / error path corrupts the exception
findings.scenario: async with browser: json.loads('x') raises JSONDecodeError, whose constructor requires (msg, doc, pos). __aexit__ runs `raise exc_type(exc_val)`, which raises "TypeError: JSONDecodeError.__init__() missing 2 required positional arguments", so `except json.JSONDecodeError` around the block never matches. An asyncio.TaskGroup failure inside the block becomes "TypeError: BaseExceptionGroup.__new__() takes exactly 2 arguments", so except* handlers miss it. Connection.__aexit__ (connection.py:599, used by `async with tab`) has the same pattern. Exceptions that keep their type also lose their attributes and traceback.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test raises inside `async with browser` or `async with tab`; the only exception test goes through conftest's CreateBrowser.
findings.repro_idea: Raise JSONDecodeError and a TaskGroup error inside `async with await zd.start()` and check which exception type escapes.
findings.evidence: Probe p5_aexit.py: 'instead got TypeError JSONDecodeError.__init__() missing 2 required positional arguments: 'doc' and 'pos'' and "instead got ['TypeError'] BaseExceptionGroup.__new__() takes exactly 2 arguments (1 given)". The fix is to return None and let Python propagate the original exception.

findings.title: Connecting to an existing browser (host+port) still requires a local Chrome binary
findings.scenario: From a slim container without Chrome, a user connects to a remote or dockerized Chrome with zd.start(host='127.0.0.1', port=9222). The docstring of util.start says 'if both host and port are provided, zendriver will not start a local chrome browser!'. Config.__init__ still calls find_executable(browser) whenever browser_executable_path is unset, which raises FileNotFoundError 'could not find a valid browser binary'. create_from_undetected_chromedriver calls Config() and has the same problem.
findings.why_tests_miss: The tests always run where Chrome is installed, and no test connects to an existing browser.
findings.repro_idea: Launch chromium with --remote-debugging-port=P, then run zd.start(host, P) under PATH=/usr/bin:/bin.
findings.evidence: Probe p9_remote.py with PATH=/usr/bin:/bin: 'connect to existing browser failed: FileNotFoundError could not find a valid browser binary...'. With chromium on PATH, the same call connects.

findings.title: Browser.stopped is True for a live browser connected through host/port, so the atexit hook skips _stop
findings.scenario: b = await zd.start(host=h, port=p) connects to a running browser with an open websocket and tabs. stopped is `not (self._process and self._process.poll() is None)`, which is always True when there is no local process. User code such as `while not browser.stopped:`, or the conftest-style `if browser is None or browser.stopped:` recreate check, treats a live browser as dead. _atexit_cleanup (`if not self.stopped: await self._stop()`) never closes this browser's connection or its ProxyForwarders.
findings.why_tests_miss: The stopped tests only cover locally launched browsers.
findings.repro_idea: Connect to an externally launched chromium and print b.stopped and len(b.tabs).
findings.evidence: Probe p9_remote.py: 'connected; stopped property says: True tabs: 1'.

findings.title: Element.get('class') and element['class'] return None for elements that have a class attribute
findings.bug_class: state-consistency / renamed key disagrees with documented API
findings.scenario: elem = await tab.select('.btn'); elem.get('class') returns None. _make_attrs stores the HTML attribute 'class' under the key 'class_', and get(name) looks up attrs.get(name) directly. Element.get's docstring says it 'Returns the value of the attribute with the given name, or None if it does not exist', and 'class_' is not documented anywhere. Code that branches on the class attribute gets the wrong result, while repr(elem) still shows class="...".
findings.why_tests_miss: test_element_get_only_returns_html_attributes checks only 'id', a missing name, and 'items'.
findings.repro_idea: Build an Element with attributes ['class','btn primary'] and compare get('class') with get('class_').
findings.evidence: In-memory probe: "get(class) -> None | get(class_) -> btn primary | e['class'] -> None | repr -> <button class=\"btn primary\" id=\"x\"></button>".

findings.title: An HTML attribute named clear/items/get/update/... shadows the ContraDict method, crashing Element.update(), repr() and get()
findings.scenario: The ContraDict docstring says names like 'keys', 'update', 'values' 'won't overwrite the methods'. Its __getattribute__ returns self[attribute] first, though, so an element whose attributes include one of these names breaks the methods zendriver calls on Element.attrs. Examples: a legacy <br clear="all"> (await elem / elem.update() / elem.query_selector_all() call self.attrs.clear() and raise TypeError: 'str' object is not callable); a custom element <x-list items="..."> (repr(elem), str(elem) and save_to_dom call attrs.items()); an attribute named get (elem.get('id') calls attrs.get()).
findings.why_tests_miss: test_element_get_only_returns_html_attributes asserts get('items') is None on an element without such an attribute; no fixture page has these attribute names.
findings.repro_idea: Build an Element with attributes ['clear','all'], ['items','x'] and ['get','x'], then call attrs.clear(), repr() and get('id').
findings.evidence: In-memory probe: "['clear', 'all'] -> TypeError 'str' object is not callable", "['items', '[1,2]'] -> TypeError 'str' object is not callable" (repr), "['get', 'x', 'id', 'a'] -> TypeError 'str' object is not callable".

findings.title: Element.__setattr__ checks key[1:] instead of '_'+key, so the Element.tree setter never runs and a bogus HTML attribute is written
findings.scenario: elem.tree = doc, the public @tree.setter that create()'s docstring points to as the alternative to update(). __setattr__ checks `key[1:] not in vars(self)`: 'ree' is not there, so the value goes into self.attrs['tree'] and _tree stays None. elem.parent then still raises 'element has no tree set', and repr(elem) and save_to_dom() write tree="Node(...)" into the page's DOM.
findings.why_tests_miss: Nothing in the code or the tests assigns elem.tree.
findings.repro_idea: Build an Element without a tree, set e.tree = doc, then print e.tree and e.attrs.
findings.evidence: In-memory probe: 'tree property after setter: None', "attrs: dict_keys(['id', 'tree'])", 'repr (what save_to_dom writes): <div id="a" tree="Node(node_id=NodeId(0)...'.

findings.title: Config.add_extension leaves the temp directory it extracts each .crx into
findings.scenario: config.add_extension('ext.crx') extracts the archive into tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='extension_'). Nothing ever removes that directory: Browser._stop and _cleanup_temporary_profile only rmtree user_data_dir. Each call, for example one Config per job in a long-running service, leaves one extracted copy in /tmp.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test calls add_extension with a file.
findings.repro_idea: Zip a minimal manifest.json into a .crx, call add_extension, start and stop a browser, and look for /tmp/extension_*.
findings.evidence: Code reading: grep shows no cleanup for the 'extension_' temp dirs, and _extensions holds only the paths. Not probed.

findings.title: Tab.save_screenshot(format='webp') crashes with UnboundLocalError when no filename is given
findings.scenario: await tab.save_screenshot(format='webp'), which is a format CDP Page.captureScreenshot accepts and that screenshot_b64 passes through. ext is set only for jpeg/jpg/png, so the default 'auto' filename branch raises UnboundLocalError: local variable 'ext' referenced before assignment, instead of saving the image or raising a clear ValueError. Element.save_screenshot initialises ext = '' and does not crash.
findings.why_tests_miss: The screenshot tests only use jpeg/png.
findings.repro_idea: Call tab.save_screenshot(format='webp') on any page.
findings.evidence: Code reading: lines 1533-1550 have no else branch setting ext before `path = pathlib.Path(candidate + ext)`. Not probed.

findings.title: Tab.__call__ passes text and selector to wait_for in swapped order, so tab(text=...) never searches by text
findings.scenario: await tab(text="Apples") (or positional await tab("Apples")) on groceries.html. __call__(text, selector, timeout) calls self.wait_for(text, selector, timeout), but the signature is wait_for(selector, text, timeout). So the text is used as a CSS selector: query_selector("Apples") polls until the timeout, then `if text:` is None and it raises TimeoutError('time ran out while waiting'). Text that is not a valid selector (e.g. "Sign up!") makes query_selector raise ProtocolException at once. tab(selector="li") only works by luck, because find_element_by_text uses DOM.performSearch, which also accepts selectors.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test in tests/ calls a Tab instance; grepping tests/ for `tab(` or `page(` finds only helper functions. test_find_* and wait_for_ready_state use other entry points.
findings.repro_idea: tab = await browser.get(sample_file('groceries.html')); await tab(text='Apples', timeout=1) raises TimeoutError, while await tab.wait_for(text='Apples', timeout=1) returns an element.
findings.evidence: Probe against real headless Chromium (detect-A12/probe1.py) printed: `call(text=Apples) raised TimeoutError time ran out while waiting`; `wait_for(text=Apples) -> script` (it finds the text); `call(selector=li) -> li 'Apples'` (works only by accident). git log -S shows the swapped call has been there since dd9a4f8 or earlier.

findings.title: remove_handlers stops tracking an auto-enabled domain but never disables it; after removing a Fetch handler every request stays paused and navigation hangs
findings.scenario: tab.add_handler(cdp.fetch.RequestPaused, h). The next send auto-enables Fetch with no patterns, so it intercepts every request, and h continues each one. Later tab.remove_handlers(cdp.fetch.RequestPaused, h) or remove_handlers(). On the next send, _register_handlers drops the empty handler list and runs `self.enabled_domains.remove(ed)` for fetch, but it never sends Fetch.disable. The browser keeps pausing every request and nothing continues them, so the next tab.get() raises TimeoutError and later evaluate() calls also time out. zendriver meanwhile reports enabled_domains == [].
findings.why_tests_miss: test_remove_handlers, test_remove_handlers_specific_event and test_remove_specific_handler assert only len(tab.handlers). They never send a command or navigate afterwards, and use Network rather than Fetch. conftest._get_shared_browser closes every tab between tests ('closing the previous tabs also drops any handlers or overrides tests added to them'), so leftover domain state never reaches a later test. intercept.py avoids the problem by sending fetch.disable() itself.
findings.repro_idea: Add an async RequestPaused handler that continues requests, then get(groceries.html) (works). remove_handlers(cdp.fetch.RequestPaused, h). get(profile.html, timeout=5) raises TimeoutError.
findings.evidence: Probe detect-A12/probe2.py printed: `with handler: paused 1 enabled [<module 'zendriver.cdp.fetch'>]`, `after remove: handlers {RequestPaused: []}`, `second nav raised TimeoutError`, `enabled_domains [] manual []`, `evaluate raised TimeoutError`. The only domain disable calls in core are the explicit ones in element.py, intercept.py and tab.py:200. _register_handlers has none.

findings.title: Sync event handlers run in a worker thread, so the documented feed_cdp() call from a handler raises RuntimeError and the paused request is never continued
findings.scenario: tab.add_handler(cdp.fetch.RequestPaused, lambda ev, conn: conn.feed_cdp(cdp.fetch.continue_request(request_id=ev.request_id))). The feed_cdp docstring describes exactly this: a non-async way to answer RequestPaused. listener_loop runs non-coroutine callbacks with asyncio.to_thread(callback, *args). Inside the worker thread, feed_cdp's asyncio.ensure_future(self.send(...)) raises 'RuntimeError: There is no current event loop in thread asyncio_0'. The send coroutine is never awaited, the request stays paused, and tab.get() times out. The only trace is an unretrieved task exception in the log.
findings.why_tests_miss: feed_cdp has no test at all. test_sync_handlers_are_each_called uses loop.call_soon_threadsafe on purpose, so it avoids the problem, and the other sync handlers in tests are no-op lambdas. examples/fetch_domain.py uses an async handler.
findings.repro_idea: Register a sync RequestPaused handler that calls conn.feed_cdp(continue_request). tab.get(sample_file('groceries.html'), timeout=5) raises TimeoutError, and stderr shows the RuntimeError traceback from ensure_future.
findings.evidence: Probe detect-A12/probe4.py printed the traceback `connection.py line 556 in feed_cdp: asyncio.ensure_future(self.send(cdp_obj)) ... RuntimeError: There is no current event loop in thread 'asyncio_0'`, then `RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'Connection.send' was never awaited` and `nav raised TimeoutError handler saw ['file:///.../groceries.html']`. Sync handlers have run in threads since 5c1a005 (#176).

findings.title: Browser.start cannot restart a browser: after stop() it reuses the stale port and info, and the 'process died' branch never launches Chrome
findings.scenario: (a) browser = await zd.start(); await browser.stop(); await browser.start(). The first start stored config.host/port, so connect_existing is True and Chrome is not launched. self.info is never cleared, so the 'Failed to connect' check passes, and Connection(old webSocketDebuggerUrl).send raises ConnectionRefusedError. (b) Chrome dies on its own, then browser.start() takes the dedicated branch `if self._process.poll() is not None: return await self.create(config=self.config)`. The new instance deep-copies a config that still holds the dead host/port, so it also skips launching and raises 'Failed to connect to browser'.
findings.why_tests_miss: tests/core/test_browser.py checks stop(), double stop() and external death (test_browser_stopped_is_true_when_stopped_externally), but never calls start() again afterwards. test_multiple_browsers_diff_userdata reuses an unstarted Config, whose port is None.
findings.repro_idea: b = await zd.start(headless=True); await b.stop(); await b.start() raises ConnectionRefusedError. Separately: b = await zd.start(); b._process.kill(); b._process.wait(); await b.start() raises Exception('Failed to connect to browser').
findings.evidence: Probe detect-A12/probe3.py printed: `stopped True host/port 127.0.0.1 51199`, `restart raised ConnectionRefusedError ["[Errno 111] Connect call failed ('127.0.0.1', 51199)"]`, and `start after external death raised Exception ['---------------------', 'Failed to connect to browser', ...]`. In start, connect_existing = host is not None and port is not None. _stop never resets config.host/port, self.info or self.connection.

findings.title: With Config.autodiscover_targets=False, every Browser.get / Tab.get(new_tab) raises TimeoutError and Tab.close times out after 10 s, even though both succeed
findings.scenario: config = zd.Config(headless=True); config.autodiscover_targets = False; browser = await zd.start(config); await browser.get(url). Browser.get waits for a Target.targetInfoChanged event and Tab.close waits for Target.targetDestroyed. Chrome only emits these after Target.setDiscoverTargets(discover=True), and start() sends that only when autodiscover_targets is set (_register_handlers skips cdp.target as 'enabled by default'). So wait_for_navigation never finishes: get() raises TimeoutError after the full timeout although the page loaded, and close() raises TimeoutError after 10 s although the tab closed.
findings.why_tests_miss: test_start_waits_for_initial_tab is the only test that sets autodiscover_targets=False, and it asserts only len(browser.tabs) == 1. It never calls get() or close().
findings.repro_idea: Start with autodiscover_targets=False. browser.get(sample_file('groceries.html'), timeout=4) raises TimeoutError, yet browser.tabs[0].evaluate('document.title') == 'Grocery List'.
findings.evidence: Probe detect-A12/probe5.py printed: `get raised TimeoutError after 4.0s`, `but page title: Grocery List`, `new_tab raised TimeoutError after 4.0s`, `close raised TimeoutError after 10.0s`. This is a different problem from the known partial-timeout issue: here the awaited event can never arrive.

findings.title: CookieJar.save/load match the pattern against str(cookie.__dict__), so patterns hit field names and enum reprs and select every cookie
findings.scenario: browser.cookies.save(file, pattern='session') to keep only cookies named like 'session_id'. The docstring says it includes cookies whose domain, key or value matches. The code runs re.finditer over str(cookie.__dict__), which contains the literal keys 'name', 'value', 'path', 'secure', 'session' and reprs such as <CookiePriority.MEDIUM: 'Medium'> and <CookieSourceScheme.SECURE: 'Secure'>. So 'session', 'secure', 'path', 'name', 'Medium' and similar patterns match every cookie, and all cookies are saved (or loaded by load(pattern=...)).
findings.why_tests_miss: test_cookies_save_writes_only_the_cookies_matching_the_pattern uses pattern='nowsecure', which matches only a value and appears in no field name or enum repr. No test uses a pattern that overlaps the dict repr, and none tests load() with a pattern.
findings.repro_idea: Set cookies 'a'(value x) and 'b'(value y); save(pattern='session'); unpickle the file: both cookies are saved although neither name, value nor domain contains 'session'.
findings.evidence: Offline probe detect-A12/probe6.py on a cdp.network.Cookie printed str(__dict__) = "{'name': 'sid', 'value': 'abc', 'domain': 'example.com', 'path': '/', ..., 'session': True, 'priority': <CookiePriority.MEDIUM: 'Medium'>, 'source_scheme': <CookieSourceScheme.SECURE: 'Secure'>...}", and the patterns session/secure/path/name/Medium all matched True. load() at line ~1067 has the same logic.

findings.title: Tab.get_all_urls(absolute=True) resolves relative links against the origin instead of the page URL and drops bare relative links
findings.scenario: On https://example.com/docs/guide/index.html, await tab.get_all_urls(). The base is built as '/'.join(self.url.rsplit('/')[:3]), i.e. just 'https://example.com'. So comes back as https://example.com/img/logo.png instead of https://example.com/docs/guide/img/logo.png. Values without '/', 'http' or '//' (e.g. 'logo.png', 'style.css?v=1') are skipped entirely, and any value containing '#' is dropped.
findings.why_tests_miss: get_all_urls and get_all_linked_sources are not referenced anywhere in tests/ (grep of tests for method names found no use).
findings.repro_idea: Serve /dir/page.html containing and call get_all_urls(): it returns ['http://host/img/a.png'], where the correct result is ['http://host/dir/img/a.png', 'http://host/dir/b.png'].
findings.evidence: Ran the exact base and filter expressions offline: `img/logo.png -> https://example.com/img/logo.png correct: https://example.com/docs/guide/img/logo.png`; `logo.png -> SKIPPED`; `style.css?v=1 -> SKIPPED`.

findings.title: Top-level array alias types whose items are $ref (Target.TargetFilter, DOMSnapshot.ArrayOfStrings) never convert their items, so typed TargetFilter values cannot be sent
findings.bug_class: wrong to_json/from_json for nested types (array alias of object refs)
findings.scenario: `await browser.connection.send(cdp.target.get_targets(filter_=cdp.target.TargetFilter([cdp.target.FilterEntry(type_="page")])))`, or the same with set_discover_targets / set_auto_attach / auto_attach_related. Generated get_targets does `params["filter"] = filter_.to_json()`. TargetFilter.to_json (zendriver/cdp/target.py:168) is `return self`, so it hands back the list of FilterEntry dataclass instances unchanged. Transaction.message then calls json.dumps, which raises `TypeError: Object of type FilterEntry is not JSON serializable`. The typed API for the filter parameter on all four Target commands is therefore unusable. The only call that works is the mis-typed `TargetFilter([{"type": "page"}])`. The reverse direction is wrong too. TargetFilter.from_json is `cls(json)`, which returns raw dicts instead of FilterEntry. DOMSnapshot.ArrayOfStrings.from_json (dom_snapshot.py:422) leaves its elements as plain ints rather than StringIndex (it is used in NodeTreeSnapshot.attributes and LayoutTreeSnapshot.styles, returned by dom_snapshot.capture_snapshot).
findings.why_tests_miss: Nothing under tests/ uses TargetFilter, FilterEntry, ArrayOfStrings or dom_snapshot, and no test exercises generated to_json/from_json directly. Zendriver core only calls set_discover_targets(discover=True) and get_targets() without a filter (browser.py:637, 784).
findings.repro_idea: With real headless Chromium: send cdp.target.get_targets(filter_=TargetFilter([FilterEntry(type_='page')])) and expect TypeError. Send the same with TargetFilter([{'type':'page'}]) and it succeeds. Also check type(TargetFilter.from_json([{'type':'page'}])[0]) is dict and isinstance(ArrayOfStrings.from_json([1])[0], StringIndex) is False. Fix: in generate_primitive_code, when items.ref is set, emit `[i.to_json() for i in self]` and `cls([Ref.from_json(i) for i in json])`.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/detect-A13/probe_filter.py against Chromium 141 printed: `to_json -> TargetFilter([FilterEntry(exclude=None, type_='page')]) FilterEntry`; `typed ERR get_targets TypeError Object of type FilterEntry is not JSON serializable`; `typed ERR set_discover_targets TypeError Object of type FilterEntry is not JSON serializable`; `dict workaround OK: ['page']`; `from_json elem type: dict`; `ArrayOfStrings elem is StringIndex: False`. Generator: the items.ref branch (lines 344-350) only builds the annotation `typing.List[FilterEntry]`, while the to_json/from_json bodies at 361-374 are identical to the scalar case. I regenerated from devtools-protocol 0.0.1612613 with a scratch copy of the generator and the output is byte-identical to zendriver/cdp, so the shipped code is exactly what the generator emits. A spec scan found only two such array-of-$ref aliases: Target.TargetFilter (items are objects) and DOMSnapshot.ArrayOfStrings (items are integer aliases).

findings.title: Generator downloads the spec into the current directory but reads it from REPO_ROOT, so running it from anywhere but the repo root deletes zendriver/cdp and fails with a misleading error
findings.bug_class: path mismatch / destructive failure / exception masking
findings.scenario: A developer runs `cd scripts && ./generate_cdp.py`, or `uv run /abs/path/scripts/generate_cdp.py` from another directory. main() checks `(REPO_ROOT/'browser_protocol.json').exists()` and gets False, then calls `dl_file(p.name)`. That runs `urllib.request.urlretrieve(url, filename='browser_protocol.json')`, a relative path, so the file lands in the current directory. main() then runs `shutil.rmtree(REPO_ROOT/'zendriver/cdp')` and opens REPO_ROOT/browser_protocol.json in parse(), which raises FileNotFoundError. The `finally:` then calls `.unlink()` on REPO_ROOT/browser_protocol.json, which raises a second FileNotFoundError that hides the first. End state: zendriver/cdp is deleted and left empty, so `import zendriver` breaks until git restores it. Both spec JSON files are left as stray files in the current directory, and the traceback points at the cleanup line rather than the real cause.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test or CI job runs scripts/generate_cdp.py; the repo has no reference to it outside the script itself. Maintainers apparently always run it from the repo root, where the current directory and REPO_ROOT are the same.
findings.repro_idea: Copy the script to a scratch tree with REPO_ROOT pointing there and a sentinel file in <root>/zendriver/cdp. Run it with the scratch scripts/ directory as the current directory. The sentinel is deleted, the JSON files appear in scripts/, and the run ends with FileNotFoundError raised from the finally block. Fix: `dl_file(p.name, p)` (or pass REPO_ROOT / name). Also make the finally block use unlink(missing_ok=True), and do the rmtree only after parsing succeeds.
findings.evidence: I ran a scratch copy (REPO_ROOT patched to /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/detect-A13/regen/root2) from root2/scripts. The traceback ended at line 1060 `list(map(lambda x: x.unlink(), json_paths))` with `FileNotFoundError: ... root2/browser_protocol.json`. Afterwards `ls root2/zendriver/cdp` showed an empty directory (the sentinel page.py was gone), and root2/scripts contained browser_protocol.json and js_protocol.json. Code: line 998 calls `dl_file(p.name)` with no path; line 1066 `filename=path or filename` is therefore relative; lines 1002-1003 do the rmtree before the try; line 1060 unlinks without missing_ok.

findings.title: Generated __repr__ on int/float alias types also changes str()/f-strings: str(NodeId(5)) == 'NodeId(5)'
findings.bug_class: wrong result from generated dunder (repr leaks into str for int/float/list/dict subclasses)
findings.scenario: `el = await tab.select('#b'); str(el.backend_node_id)` returns 'BackendNodeId(6)', not '6'. `wid, _ = await tab.get_window(); f'{wid}'` returns 'WindowID(1190458396)'. The generator overrides only __repr__. int and float have no __str__ of their own, so str(), '%s' and an empty format spec all fall through to that __repr__. Affected classes: NodeId, BackendNodeId, WindowID, ExecutionContextId, StringIndex, CertificateId, network/input/runtime/media TimeSinceEpoch, MonotonicTime, Timestamp and TimeDelta (12 classes), plus the list/dict aliases (Headers, Quad). So any user code that stringifies an id or timestamp gets wrong text: logging, building a JS snippet or selector, or writing ids to a file and later calling int() on them (ValueError). Zendriver's own debug log does it too (cloudflare.py:169 logs 'node_id: NodeId(5)'). str subclasses such as FrameId are unaffected because str defines __str__.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test stringifies a CDP id or timestamp. Ids are only compared with == (which works) or passed back to CDP via json.dumps, which uses int.__repr__/float.__repr__ of the base type and so serializes correctly.
findings.repro_idea: assert str(zendriver.cdp.dom.NodeId(5)) == '5' fails, and f'{cdp.network.MonotonicTime(1.5)}' == '1.5' fails. Fix: also emit `def __str__(self): return super().__repr__()` for int/float aliases, or emit __repr__ only (keeping super().__str__) by delegating str to the base type.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/detect-A13/probe_str.py against Chromium 141 printed: `str(el.backend_node_id) = BackendNodeId(6) | f'{wid}' = WindowID(1190458396) | json: {"w": 1190458396}` and `int(str(id)) -> ValueError invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'BackendNodeId(6)'`. An offline check printed `NodeId(5) NodeId(5) NodeId(5) TimeSinceEpoch(1.5) TimeSinceEpoch(1.5) abc ExecutionContextId(3)` for str / f-string / %s on NodeId and TimeSinceEpoch and str() on FrameId. Generated example: zendriver/cdp/dom.py BackendNodeId.__repr__ (around lines 49-50).

findings.title: Optional 'any'-typed fields treat None as 'omit', so CallArgument cannot pass JavaScript null (it arrives as undefined)
findings.bug_class: None/null conflation in to_json for optional any-typed values
findings.scenario: `await tab.send(cdp.runtime.call_function_on('function(x){return x===null}', object_id=..., arguments=[cdp.runtime.CallArgument(value=None)], return_by_value=True))` returns false, and typeof x is 'undefined'. For every optional property the generator emits `if self.value is not None: json['value'] = ...`. For a field typed `any` (Runtime.CallArgument.value at runtime.py:577, also RemoteObject.value and DeepSerializedValue.value), None is the natural Python spelling of JSON null, but it is dropped. The CDP spec says an empty CallArgument means undefined. The typed API therefore cannot express null as a primitive value. The only workaround is the undocumented UnserializableValue('null'), whose spec only lists -0, NaN, Infinity, -Infinity and bigint literals.
findings.why_tests_miss: No test builds a CallArgument with value=; zendriver core only uses CallArgument(object_id=...) (element.py:431, 505, 991; tab.py:1463).
findings.repro_idea: call_function_on('function(x){return arguments.length+":"+(x===null?"null":typeof x)}', arguments=[CallArgument(value=None)]) returns '1:undefined'. Fix: for any-typed optional fields use a sentinel default, distinct from None, to mean 'omitted'.
findings.evidence: Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-zendriver/b2021b39-94e6-5220-9e66-7f33c0314a80/scratchpad/detect-A13/probe_null.py against Chromium 141 printed: `CallArgument(value=None).to_json() -> {}`, `value=None -> 1:undefined`, `value=0 -> 1:number`, `value='' -> 1:string`, and `unserializable null -> 1:null`. Falsy values (0, '') are correctly kept, so only null is lost. Low confidence because this follows from the generator's None-means-absent convention, and a workaround exists.
